page: Amazon Web Services m9g.8xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V3 processor based on the ARMv9 family. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz, with a cache hierarchy consisting of 64 KB L1D, 2 MB L2, and 48 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 17 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics, software compilation with Clang, and text processing. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, also rank in the top tier. Passmark database operations and memory scores are highly rated, while Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput show strong performance. However, LLM inference tasks present mixed results, with text generation using a small 135M model falling into the bottom tier, while prompt processing and medium 7B model generation remain average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m9g.8xlarge leverages the ARMv9 architecture to deliver high resource density and strong multi-threaded performance per unit of compute. The absence of simultaneous multithreading means each of the 32 vCPUs is a dedicated physical core, reducing resource contention. This hardware profile is suited for workloads such as software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing, though it is less optimal for intensive LLM text generation tasks.
